title: E2 agreement and reference checkpoint form A
instructions: Choose the only sentence with controlled agreement or unambiguous reference. Complete all five before submitting.

parts.prompt: Which sentence correctly controls agreement despite the interrupting phrase?

options.text: The set of emergency instructions are beside the door.
The set of emergency instructions is beside the door.
The set of emergency instructions have been beside the door.
The set of emergency instructions remain beside the door.

choice_rationales.A: Instructions is inside an of-phrase and does not control the verb.
choice_rationales.B: The singular head noun set correctly takes is.
choice_rationales.C: Have follows the nearby plural noun rather than the head subject.
choice_rationales.D: Remain is plural and does not agree with set.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: Remove the of-phrase: the set is beside the door.

parts.prompt: Complete the sentence: ‘One of the solar lamps ___ a damaged switch.’

options.text: have
were having
are having
has

choice_rationales.A: Lamps is not the head subject.
choice_rationales.B: The plural auxiliary does not agree with one.
choice_rationales.C: The plural auxiliary follows the nearby noun incorrectly.
choice_rationales.D: The singular head one takes has.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: One is the grammatical controller, so the verb must be singular.

parts.prompt: Which sentence correctly treats two distinct people as a compound subject?

options.text: The curator and her assistant are checking the labels.
The curator and her assistant is checking the labels.
The curator and her assistant checks the labels.
The curator and her assistant has checked the labels separately yesterday.

choice_rationales.A: Two distinct subjects joined by and take plural agreement.
choice_rationales.D: Has is singular and the time phrase conflicts with the construction.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: The curator and the assistant are two people, so are is required.

parts.prompt: Aisha lent her calculator to Nur, and Nur discovered a loose key. Which revision makes the discoverer and object unambiguous?

options.text: When Aisha lent it to Nur, she discovered that it was loose.
Aisha lent her calculator to Nur because she found her key loose.
After Aisha lent Nur the calculator, Nur discovered that one of the calculator's keys was loose.
After she lent it to her, she discovered its loose key.

choice_rationales.A: She could refer to Aisha or Nur, and it has competing referents.
choice_rationales.B: She and her do not identify the intended person or object clearly.
choice_rationales.C: Both the discoverer and the damaged object are explicitly named.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: Repeating the relevant names and noun phrase prevents competing antecedents.

parts.prompt: A storm damaged the notice, not the gate. Which sentence communicates that meaning most clearly?

options.text: The notice was attached to the gate when it was damaged.
The storm damaged the notice that had been attached to the gate.
It damaged it beside it.
The gate held the notice before it happened to it.

choice_rationales.A: It could refer to the notice or the gate.
choice_rationales.B: The verb directly names the notice as the damaged object.
choice_rationales.C: The pronouns have no stable antecedents.
choice_rationales.D: Both uses of it are unclear.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: Placing notice directly after damaged removes the reference ambiguity.
